NEW DELHI: PM Narendra Modi said on Friday he will forgive young protesters accused of abusing him and his late mother, saying they are misguided children and it is “our job to show them the right way”.In a video message, Modi said punishing these youth and making them run around courts will not change circumstances, adding that these children have lost their way and must be guided instead of being subjected to any harassment. His comments came amid incidents of criminal cases being lodged against some young protesters for abusing him during the recent student protest. “Everybody saw what happened at Jantar Mantar,” the PM said.They abused not only me but also my late mother. It was such a vile thing. But I want to say today that mistakes happen at a young age, and this is also the opportunity to correct those mistakes,” he said. “I want to forgive them. Society should also accept my decision,” he said in a clear indication that cases against these youngsters will be withdrawn. Modi as Gujarat CM had forgiven a youngster accused of sending a threatening mail to him, sources said.

NEW DELHI: Jan Suraaj Party (JSP) founder Prashant Kishor has finally found a seat for his “school bag” in Bihar. The election strategist-turned-politician, whose party contests on a school bag symbol, has flipped the Bankipur assembly seat, an unassailable bastion of the BJP for the last 30 years. Before today’s shock defeat, the BJP had registered 8 consecutive victories in Bankipur since 1995, when it won the seat for the first time.By-election in Bankipur was necessitated after Nitin Nabin resigned as BJP MLA from the seat in April after his election to Rajya Sabha. This followed Nitin Nabin’s elevation as BJP national president in January this year.To gauge the enormity of Prashant Kishor’s victory, look at these facts:For PK, as Prashant Kishor is popularly known, contesting the Bankipur byelection was a huge political gamble. PK, who made a high-pitched entry into Bihar politics with a padyatra spanning months ahead of the 2025 assembly elections, cut a sorry figure when his Jan Suraj Party failed to win even one seat less than a year ago. Such dismal was his first electoral show that JSP lost deposit in 236 of the 238 seats it contested. Prashant Kishor did not contest the election himself and instead led a high-voltage campaign for his party across the state.Little wonder his decision to contest the Bankipur bypoll was fraught with the danger of becoming a make-or-break political move. But the gamble has paid off and Prashant Kishor with his debut win has propelled into the centrestage of Bihar politics.Prashant Kishor polled over 64,151 votes and won the key electoral battle by a margin of 19,324 votes over BJP’s Neeraj Kumar. Prashant Kishor’s resounding success, nine months after his party’s humiliating defeat, marks a remarkable turnaround.And making the most of his victory, Prashant Kishor immediately trained his guns at Bihar chief minister Samrat Choudhary."This is the victory of the people of Bankipur. As we stated during the election campaign, this was not just an election to choose an MLA. It was an attempt by the people of Bihar to send a message to the BJP's central leadership that they should appoint a good person as the chief minister of Bihar. They do not want a person with a criminal background or questionable conduct, character, or reputation to lead Bihar. They want a good chief minister who can improve education, create employment opportunities for the youth, and ensure that the children of Bihar do not have to migrate elsewhere for work," Kishor told reporters as his supporters celebrated his maiden electoral victory.Prashant Kishor’s use of his victory to target Samrat Choudhary did not come as a surprise. Ksihor been unrelenting in his attacks against the BJP leader ever since the election strategist became a full-time politician. He has targeted Samrat Choudhary over the chief minister’s educational qualification and his alleged criminal past.The Jan Suraaj chief also called upon the BJP's central leadership to focus on governance ahead of the next Lok Sabha elections, stating, "Before the Lok Sabha elections, Prime Minister Modi, the BJP, and Amit Shah should focus on improving Bihar, creating jobs for its youth, and stopping migration. That is our only objective. We do not want to become MLAs merely to award contracts. Our sole objective is the development of Bihar. "These are the very themes on which Prashant Kishor fought the 2025 assembly elections and lost. Clearly, while he keeps focus on these issues, his victory in bankipur may less be about endorsement of his development focus and more about people’s disappointment with the BJP. The result is also perhaps a fallout of the students’ agitation against NEET-UG paper leak, which saw huge protests in Bihar. In Siwan, a police constable was suspended after a video purportedly showing him using an AK-47 rifle during a student protest on July 25 went viral on social media.Leader of opposition in Bihar assembly, Tejashwi Yadav , slammed Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary for the incident. He posted a video of the purported incident on X and, along with it, said, "During the protest in Siwan, police resorted to direct firing with an AK-47 on students. When a criminal becomes chief minister, then police fire bullets at innocent students.”CPI(ML) Liberation general secretary Dipankar Bhattacharya in his message to Prashant Kishor described his victory as a significant verdict by Bihar's youth against the BJP-led state government.In a post on X, Bhattacharya termed Kishor's victory a "well-earned debut victory" and said the bypoll result reflected public anger against the ruling dispensation."Congratulations to Prashant Kishor on his well-earned debut victory in Bankipur bypoll. Kudos to the youth of Bihar for delivering such a telling blow to the supremely arrogant, incompetent and tyrannical BJP government of Bihar," he said.The BJP was quick to accept the verdict of the people. State BJP president Sanjay Saraogi said in a statement, "We bow before the will of the people. We shall draw lessons from the debacle, unlike our opponents who tend to blame every electoral loss of theirs on EVMs and the Election Commission".But for the BJP, this defeat comes as an embarrassment for both its national president Nitin Nabin and the party’s first chief minister in the state Samrat Choudhary. Bankipur seat was literally a personal fiefdom of Nitin Nabin’s family which represented the constituency for 30 long years. A defeat in the backyard will surely embarrass the BJP chief.For Samrat Choudhary, this was the first electoral test of his government which was formed after the BJP took over the reins of the state from JD(U) chief Nitish Kumar. It was Nitish Kumar who had led the NDA to an emphatic triumph in the 2025 assembly elections. And the BJP would have hoped that Samrat Choudhary would have given it a winning start. But that was not to be.The Bankipur bypoll result also has a worrying message for the main opposition party RJD. Tejashwi Yadav’s party seems to have learnt no lessons from the 2025 electoral drubbing. The party which has been reduced to 25 seats in the assembly did little to show intent on the ground.Its candidate Rekha Kumari polled just 14,273 votes. This was over 32,000 votes less than the figure of 46,363, which she had polled in the 2025 assembly elections as the runnerup in the seat. Ironically, for the greater part of the campaign, RJD’s star campaigner Tejashwi Yadav was missing in action.It may not be prudent to overexaggerate the outcome of one bypoll. The result of one seat, even though high-profile, may not be indicative of any larger trend. But for the BJP and the RJD to brush aside the defeat as a one-off setback would be doing harm to their cause. The BJP should remember that it rules Bihar but is still dependent on its allies for survival. The RJD, meanwhile, remains the main opposition party but seems to have lost the plot to factionalism and family feuds after its dismal 2025 show. Both need to pause and review what went wrong in Bankipur. MLA Prashant Kishor, on the other hand, will perhaps be now preparing for another bout with his political bete noir Samrat Choudhary - this time on the floor of Bihar assembly.
Article Summary: Jan Suraaj Party (JSP) founder Prashant Kishor has finally found a seat for his “school bag” in Bihar. The election strategist-turned-politician has flipped the Bankipur assembly seat, an unassailable bastion of the BJP for the last 30 years. Before today’s shock defeat, the BJP had registered 8 consecutive victories in the seat.

NEW DELHI: Jan Suraaj founder Prashant Kishor on Monday won the Bankipur assembly bypoll, defeating BJP candidate Neeraj Kumar by 19,324 votes after securing 64,151 votes, marking a winning start to his electoral career.The bypoll, necessitated after BJP national president Nitin Nabin vacated the seat following his election to the Rajya Sabha, turned into much more than a contest for a single constituency. Bankipur had remained one of the BJP's safest urban seats for over three decades, with Nabin winning it four consecutive times by comfortable margins.Kishor's victory in the BJP's long-held bastion is likely to be seen as one of the biggest political upsets in Bihar after the assembly elections defeat. BJP's Neeraj Kumar secured 44,827 votes, while RJD candidate Rekha Kumari finished a distant third with 14,273 votes.Bankipur marks Prashant Kishor's biggest electoral breakthrough since entering active politics and launching the Jan Suraaj Party. The victory is particularly significant because it came in a constituency long regarded as a BJP bastion.The win marks a dramatic turnaround for Kishor. In the 2025 Bihar assembly elections , Jan Suraaj contested 238 seats but failed to win a single one, securing just a 3.44% vote share. In 68 constituencies, the party polled fewer votes than the NOTA option. The Bankipur victory signals improvement in the party's electoral fortunes and strengthens Kishor's claim of emerging as a credible political alternative in Bihar ahead of the next assembly election.For the BJP, the result is significant because Bankipur has long been among its strongest urban constituencies. Nitin Nabin won the seat in 2010, 2015, 2020 and 2025, each time by comfortable margins.In the 2025 assembly election, Nabin secured 98,299 votes, a 63.25% vote share, defeating the RJD candidate by 51,936 votes. Losing such a seat raises questions about the BJP's ability to retain its traditional urban support base and could prompt a reassessment of its campaign strategy in the next assembly elections.The result carries personal significance for BJP national president Nitin Nabin, who vacated the Bankipur seat after being elected to the Rajya Sabha. The constituency has been synonymous with his political career, with Nabin representing it continuously since 2015 and turning it into one of the BJP's strongest urban bastions in Bihar.Less than a year after Nabin registered a landslide victory in Bankipur, the BJP has lost the seat under his tenure as national president. The defeat is likely to raise questions about the party's organisational strength in his home turf and provide the opposition with an opportunity to challenge the BJP leadership's grip over one of its safest constituencies.The Bankipur bypoll has also exposed the RJD's inability to emerge as the principal challenger in a high-profile contest. Despite fielding Rekha Kumari, the party finished a distant third, with the election effectively turning into a direct fight between the BJP and Prashant Kishor.The result is likely to raise uncomfortable questions for Tejashwi Yadav, who has projected himself as the NDA's chief challenger in Bihar. His absence from the campaign also became a political issue, with NDA leaders, including Union minister Chirag Paswan, accusing him of remaining abroad during the bypoll. The outcome is likely to fuel speculation that sections of the anti-BJP electorate are looking beyond the RJD, with Prashant Kishor emerging as a potential alternative opposition face.The biggest political implication may lie beyond the bypoll itself. Jan Suraaj's victory in Bankipur strengthens the argument that Bihar's politics may no longer remain confined to the NDA versus the RJD-led Mahagathbandhan contest.While one bypoll alone cannot establish a statewide trend, defeating the BJP in one of its strongest constituencies significantly boosts Jan Suraaj's credibility. The result could encourage voters seeking an alternative to the two established alliances and make Prashant Kishor's party a more consequential player in the upcoming Bihar assembly elections.
Article Summary: Jan Suraaj founder Prashant Kishor on Monday won the Bankipur assembly bypoll, defeating BJP candidate Neeraj Kumar by 19,324 votes. The bypoll was necessitated after BJP national president Nitin Nabin vacated the seat following his election to the Rajya Sabha. The result raises questions about the BJP's ability to retain its traditional urban support base.

NEW DELHI: In the recently-concluded Commonwealth Games 2026 in Glasgow, Indian military personnel have a lion’s share in winning medals for the country. The Indian Army won 16 medals of India's total medal haul of 39. Two Indian Navy personnel also won medals. If the medals won by Army and Navy personnel are combined, the services personnel bagged 18 medals out of the total 39, which is equivalent to 46% contribution of the services in winning medals.“A contingent of 20 Indian Army athletes won 16 medals for the Nation”, the Army said, adding out of 16 medals, eight are gold, seven silver and one bronze.Praising its personnel, the Indian Army, in a post X on Monday, said, “Har Kaam, Desh Ke Naam. General Dhiraj Seth, COAS and All Ranks of Indian Army extend heartiest congratulations to the Indian Army athletes for their outstanding performance at the Commonwealth Games Glasgow 2026. ”Giving details of the disciplines were the Armymen won laurels, the ADG PI said, “Indian Army athletes exceptional performance is testimony of their zeal and commitment across judo, boxing, athletics, para athletics and weightlifting. Their achievements reaffirm the Indian Army's steadfast commitment to nurturing world-class athletes and advancing the Nation's sporting aspirations through Mission Olympics 2036.The Army gave details of its Army personnel winning medals: Gold medals won by Havildar Harsh in judo (60 kg), Naib Subedar Preeti in boxing (54 kg); Naib Subedar Jaismine in boxing (57 kg); Subedar Soman Rana in para shot put; Havildar Sakshi in boxing (51 kg); Havildar Arundhati in boxing (70 kg); Havildar Sachin in boxing (60 kg) and Havildar Ankush in boxing (80 kg).Silver medals have been won by Naib Subedar Sarvesh in high jump; Nb Sub Gulveer in 10,000 m; Hav Ajaya Babu in weightlifting; Lt Col (Honorary) Neeraj Chopra in javelin throw; Hav Jadumani in boxing; Lance Naik Shubham Juyal in para shot put and Sub Narender in boxing (+90 kg). Bronze medal has been won by Nb Sub Gulveer in the 5,000-m track.Two Navy personnel — Chief Petty Officer Communication (Telegraphist) Lovepreet Singh and Chief Petty Officer (PT) Chanambam Rishikanta Singh — won silver medals in weightlifting category. In a post on X, the Navy said, “Indian Navy's Lovepreet Singh, CPO COM (TEL), powered to a SILVER medal in the +110 kg Weightlifting category at CWG2026! Total Lift of 388 kg (176 kg Snatch + 212 kg Clean & Jerk). Rewriting the history books with a 176 kg Snatch, setting a new Commonwealth Games Record! Lovepreet ! You've made the nation proud. ”

Some of them operated from special economic zones.An inter-governmental body like the Financial Action Task Force, the Sydney-based APG initiated this study led by Indonesia and UN Office on Drugs and Crime with a team comprised of 24 experts from the govts of Australia, Bangladesh, China, India, Indonesia, Malaysia, Myanmar, Solomon Islands, Singapore, Vietnam and UAE.The study examined the emerging nexus between human trafficking and cyber-enabled financial crime, drawing upon the debriefings of 15 Indian nationals repatriated from Myanmar, Lao PDR, and Cambodia between 2023 and 2024.The individuals were recruited under the pretext of high-paying customer-service or IT jobs, transported through Thailand, and then coerced to work in criminal “scam compounds” operated by transnational syndicates, it said.“Victims were mostly young men (20-35 age group) from nine Indian states, recruited via social media or personal networks, who paid upfront fees (Rs 50-70,000). Compounds were run by Chinese-speaking syndicates, with multi-national workforces and strict control (passport confiscation, physical/psychological abuse),” the report has said.The report further revealed that these slave workers were sold between scam compounds, where they were subjected to confinement, violence and debt bondage. “Interception operations and large-scale rescues have revealed victims from a variety of nationalities and regions, suggesting that recruitment practices have expanded beyond solely regional contexts. In one case, muule bank accounts and SIM cards from Punjab were supplied to cyber fraudsters in the Philippines, facilitating scams totalling over Rs 40 crore. Article Title: How Prashant Kishor breached BJP's bastion
Article Text:
Prashant Kishor broke the BJP's three-decade hold on Bankipur and reshaped Bihar's political landscape.

The fall of a BJP fortress

From electoral debut disaster to historic victory

A changing political mood

Why youth turned towards Prashant Kishor

Tejashwi Yadav's absence created political space

Core voters turned away from the BJP, RJD

BJP's candidate switch added to the narrative

The first electoral verdict after the nationwide Gen Z protests has delivered one of the biggest political surprises in recent years. BJP has lost Bankipur, one of its safest seats in Bihar, to Prashant Kishor , giving Jan Suraaj its first-ever electoral victory.The result carries significance beyond a single assembly bypoll. It is also the first major electoral test for BJP in Bihar under the leadership of CM Samrat Choudhary after he assumed charge of the state government. The outcome suggests that the party failed to retain its grip over a constituency that had remained virtually impregnable for three decades.Bankipur has been synonymous with BJP's dominance since 1995. The party won the seat four consecutive times through Navin Sinha before his son, BJP national president Nitin Nabin, retained it for five successive elections.The constituency had long been regarded as one of BJP's safest urban seats. Nitin Nabin secured more than 50% of the vote in every election he contested, including around 63% in the 2025 Assembly election. Against that backdrop, the bypoll result represents a dramatic political reversal.The bypoll attracted unusual national attention largely because Prashant Kishor decided to contest personally.Only nine months ago, Jan Suraaj had suffered a crushing setback in the Bihar Assembly elections . The party fielded candidates in 238 of the state's 243 constituencies but failed to win a single seat, while forfeiting deposits in 236 constituencies. Despite an extensive campaign built around Prashant Kishor's personal credibility, the party could not convert public attention into votes.The obvious question, therefore, is: what changed in just nine months?Political observers believe the 2025 Assembly election was heavily influenced by welfare promises, including direct financial assistance for women and free electricity, helping the NDA secure a decisive victory. Since then, Bihar's political environment appears to have shifted considerably.The transition from Nitish Kumar to Samrat Choudhary as Chief Minister coincided with a series of developments that reportedly generated dissatisfaction among sections of BJP's traditional support base. Controversies surrounding the UGC guidelines, the Bharat Tiwari encounter, and widespread anger over repeated paper leak incidents created fresh political fault lines, particularly among students and young voters.Education has remained at the centre of Prashant Kishor's political messaging. His repeated emphasis on education reforms appears to have resonated with young voters seeking systemic change.He has consistently questioned the academic credentials of Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary while projecting education reform as one of Bihar's most urgent priorities. His image as an educated professional has helped him emerge as a credible alternative, especially among urban youth.Following the nationwide Gen Z protests, Bihar witnessed some of the strongest student mobilisations over paper leak controversies. While the state has made visible improvements in roads and infrastructure over the past decade, concerns over the quality of education and the continued migration of young people remain widespread.For many first-time and young voters, Prashant Kishor increasingly appeared to represent change.Equally significant was the growing disappointment among sections of the opposition's traditional support base.Many voters expected Leader of the Opposition Tejashwi Yadav to aggressively raise issues affecting students and other public concerns. According to political observers in Patna, his perceived lack of visibility during debates over the Bharat Tiwari encounter and student protests created a vacuum in opposition politics.Many voters reportedly believed that while one bypoll would not alter the government's stability, electing Prashant Kishor would strengthen the opposition's voice inside the Assembly.The final extent of vote transfer will become clearer only after the Election Commission releases detailed voting data. However, reporters on the ground believe Prashant Kishor attracted support from both BJP's and RJD's traditional voter bases.RJD candidate Rekha Kumari appears to have suffered the sharpest decline. After securing 46,363 votes in the 2025 Assembly election, she is now estimated to have polled fewer than 15,000 votes.There are also indications that sections of BJP's upper-caste support base were unhappy over issues such as paper leaks, the UGC guidelines and the Bharat Tiwari encounter.The BJP's last-minute change of candidate also became a major talking point during the campaign. The party's nominee, Abhishek Kumar Sinha, withdrew his nomination on July 10 citing personal reasons. The withdrawal came just hours after Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary had campaigned for him in Bankipur.BJP subsequently fielded Neeraj Kumar Sinha, who was widely perceived as a weaker candidate. Prashant Kishor seized on the development, arguing that the BJP was struggling to find a suitable candidate because voters now had a credible alternative.
Article Summary: Bankipur has been synonymous with BJP's dominance since 1995. The party won the seat four consecutive times through Navin Sinha before his son, BJP national president Nitin Nabin, retained it for five successive elections. The outcome suggests that the party failed to retain its grip over a constituency that had remained virtually impregnable for three decades.

Luka Doncic says the hamstring injury that ended his 2025-26 season is fully behind him, with training camp now the next stop on the Los Angeles Lakers' calendar. In an email to fans relayed by The Athletic's Dan Woike, Doncic confirmed his offseason rehab is complete. The update carries weight because his absence exposed how much the Lakers' offense leaned on him last spring, and it lands just as the roster around him has been almost entirely rebuilt.Luka Doncic suffered a Grade 2 strain in his left hamstring on April 2, an injury that shut down his regular season and ruled him out for the playoffs. Woike reported that further evaluation in Spain found more damage than the original imaging suggested, sending Doncic overseas for treatment. ESPN's Dave McMenamin reported he was cleared for basketball activities on May 28, roughly two weeks after the Lakers' playoff run ended."My recovery went great, and I'm 100% healthy again," Doncic wrote to fans, adding that stepping away from the game each summer is part of his usual routine and tends to leave him more motivated once he returns."I took a real break from basketball the first few weeks after the season ended to rehab my body.My recovery went great, and I’m 100% healthy again," Doncic shared in the email.The Lakers superstar went on to add, "Taking some time away from basketball is something I do at the start of every offseason. It’s a different way to do things, but it works for me. When I let myself miss the game a little bit and try some new things, it only makes me more excited and motivated to get back to playing."The injury's cost was visible in the numbers. Los Angeles posted a 119.4 offensive rating with Doncic on the floor last season against 111.9 with him off it, based on NBA.com tracking, and the gap showed up in a second-round sweep to Oklahoma City. Doncic still won his second career scoring title at 33.5 points per game, adding 7.7 rebounds and 8.3 assists.That production now carries more weight with LeBron James gone to Philadelphia. The Lakers also lost Rui Hachimura, Marcus Smart, Luke Kennard and Jaxson Hayes in free agency and traded Deandre Ayton to Washington, replacing them with nine new additions including Walker Kessler, Quentin Grimes and Collin Sexton. Austin Reaves re-signed on a four-year deal, leaving him, Doncic and Kessler as the roster's core.Not everyone is convinced Doncic still ranks among the position's best. Vaughn Alexander, father of Thunder guard Shai Gilgeous-Alexander, used a weekend livestream to list his top three point guards: his son first, Detroit's Cade Cunningham second, and Memphis' Ja Morant third. He argued that defense should factor into any such ranking, noting Doncic has been an MVP-level scorer but has work to do on the other end."He's in the MVP conversation every year. He's top three," Alexander said of Doncic, before pointing to Gilgeous-Alexander's steals numbers as the kind of two-way standard he believes should count.Doncic isn't waiting for that debate to settle before getting to work. He's invited the full Lakers roster, including two-way players, to Slovenia for a four-day minicamp this month, with workouts alongside golf and sightseeing in Ljubljana built into the schedule. Training camp opens in late September, with media day expected around September 29. This time, Doncic plans to be the one setting the tone from the start.
Article Summary: Luka Doncic says he's "100% healthy again" after recovering from a hamstring injury. The Slovenian won the NBA scoring title last season, scoring 33.5 points per game. His absence exposed how much the Lakers' offense leaned on him last spring. Training camp opens in late September.

BENGALURU: What began as a controversy over the Indian hockey team’s switch from its traditional blue jersey to saffron has now snowballed into a governance battle within Hockey India (HI).In a strongly worded letter to the federation’s director general (DG), Cdr RK Srivastava, HI president Dilip Tirkey has raised serious questions over authority, accountability and transparency in the decision-making process behind the jersey change.The letter, accessed by TOI, is Tirkey’s response to Srivastava’s July 31 explanation on the approval process. Questioning who authorised the redesign and whether due process was followed, Tirkey has sought answers from the federation’s administrative leadership, deepening the controversy.Describing the DG’s four-page reply as largely off the point, Tirkey wrote: “...the issue under consideration is not merely the colour or design of a playing jersey. The matter concerns the decision-making process adopted for a change involving one of the most recognisable symbols of Indian hockey, the authority under which such a decision was taken, the consultations undertaken, compliance with Hockey India’s governance framework, and whether appropriate institutional processes were followed.The former India captain added: “Hockey India is a custodian of a legacy. Decisions affecting such symbols must therefore be approached with the highest standards of governance, transparency and accountability.”Tirkey also questioned why the elected Executive Board was bypassed. Revealing that he learnt about the redesigned jersey only through a WhatsApp group message a few hours before its social media launch on July 27, Tirkey wrote: “The Director General has an important executive and administrative role in managing the affairs of Hockey India and implementing approved decisions. However, administrative responsibility cannot be interpreted as replacing or overriding the authority of the elected governance bodies. Given the importance and national significance of the decision, the Executive Board requires clarification as to why the President and the Executive Board were not consulted before the public announcement.”The 412-cap India veteran also took exception to a section of the DG’s reply that detailed HI’s high-performance initiatives.“The Executive Board is fully familiar with the demands of elite sport and high-performance environments. The EB includes several distinguished former international players and Olympians who have personally experienced the demands of preparing for and performing at the highest levels of hockey... and fully recognises that modern sport requires continuous improvement and that every genuine marginal gain must be pursued,” Tirkey wrote.With the controversy erupting less than three weeks before the FIH Hockey World Cup begins in the Netherlands and Belgium on Aug 15, Tirkey also questioned the timing of the change.“A decision intended to improve performance must not inadvertently create uncertainty, distraction or disruption at a critical stage of preparation. It is therefore necessary for the Executive Board to understand how the jersey change was assessed within the overall high-performance plan,” he said.Tirkey has sought a comprehensive reply from the DG, supported by documentary evidence, by 5 pm on Tuesday.Signing off, he wrote: “Hockey India does not own Indian hockey. We are trustees and custodians of a national sporting legacy”.
Article Summary: Dilip Tirkey has raised serious questions over authority, accountability and transparency in the decision-making process behind the jersey change. Tirkey also questioned the timing of the change. The controversy erupts less than three weeks before the FIH Hockey World Cup begins in the Netherlands and Belgium.

Article Title: Meet Nathan Thomas: 18-year-old Florida teen becomes the world's youngest male professor after breaking a 306-year-old record

How Nathan Thomas became the world's youngest male professor

An inspiration for young learners

At an age when many students are just beginning university, Nathan Thomas had already stepped into the classroom as a college professor. The Florida native earned a place in the Guinness World Records after becoming the world's youngest male professor at just 18 years and 346 days old, breaking a record that had stood for 306 years. Thomas joined Miami Dade College as an engineering instructor, where he teaches students who are often close to his own age. His remarkable academic journey, which began with enrolling in college at the age of 10, has now made him one of the youngest educators ever to teach at the higher education level. His journey stands out not only for the record itself but for what it represents, a reminder that intellectual growth does not always follow a fixed timeline, and that curiosity, nurtured early, can open doors.Nathan Thomas officially became the world's youngest male professor when he accepted an engineering teaching position at Miami Dade College at the age of 18 years and 346 days. Guinness World Records confirmed that he surpassed the record previously held by Scottish mathematician Colin Maclaurin, who became a professor at the age of 19 in 1717. The achievement ended a record that had remained unbeaten for more than three centuries.Thomas began teaching COP 2270: C for Engineers at Miami Dade College in August 2023. The course introduces engineering students to the fundamentals of C programming and computational problem-solving. Many of his students are around the same age as him, but Thomas believes age matters far less than a willingness to learn. He has said that everyone enters the classroom with the same goal of gaining knowledge and improving their skills. His appointment also demonstrates that expertise and dedication, rather than age alone, can earn respect in higher education.Thomas displayed exceptional academic ability from an early age. At just 10 years old, he dual-enrolled at Miami Dade College while continuing his school education. By the age of 14, he had transferred to Florida International University, where he completed both bachelor's and master's degrees in electrical engineering with honours. His accelerated academic path eventually led him back to Miami Dade College, this time as a faculty member rather than a student.Coming from a family of engineers, Thomas developed an interest in mathematics and science at a young age. He has credited his mother with helping him understand mathematical concepts in ways that made learning enjoyable. He says the most rewarding part of teaching is watching students grasp ideas that once seemed difficult, describing those moments as just as satisfying as solving engineering problems himself.While continuing to teach, Thomas is also pursuing a Juris Doctor degree at the University of Miami School of Law, with an expected graduation in 2028. He hopes to combine his engineering background with legal expertise by specialising in intellectual property law, particularly in areas involving science, technology, engineering and mathematics. According to Thomas, the structured problem-solving skills he developed through engineering have proved valuable in his legal studies. By bridging engineering and law, he hopes to contribute to the protection of innovation in rapidly evolving fields driven by science and technology.Nathan Thomas's achievement demonstrates how determination, curiosity and a passion for learning can open extraordinary opportunities at a young age. From entering college as a child to becoming the world's youngest male professor and breaking a 306-year-old Guinness World Record, his journey has inspired students and educators alike. As he continues balancing teaching with law school, Thomas hopes to contribute to both education and innovation while encouraging others to pursue ambitious goals regardless of age.
Article Summary: Nathan Thomas became the world's youngest male professor at the age of 18 years and 346 days. The record had been held by Scottish mathematician Colin Maclaurin, who became a professor at 19 in 1717. Thomas is also pursuing a Juris Doctor degree at the University of Miami School of Law.

NEW DELHI: T Dilip signed off from his role as India's fielding coach with an emotional farewell message on Monday, bringing the curtain down on a memorable five-year stint that transformed the team's fielding culture and coincided with one of its most successful eras across formats.Having joined the national set-up in November 2021, the Hyderabad-based coach departed after his contract was not renewed following India's T20I tour of Zimbabwe. Subhadeep Ghosh has replaced him as the fielding coach and will travel with the team for the upcoming two-Test series against Sri Lanka beginning on August 15."It is difficult to find the right words for a journey that has meant so much," Dilip wrote in a heartfelt Instagram post that reflected on his time with the team."When I first walked into this setup, I came in with one simple intention, to give everything I had every single day. Fielding has always been my way of contributing to the game I love, and I'm grateful for the opportunity to have played a part in this team's journey."Among the many memories Dilip revisited, none stood out more than the now-iconic fielding medal ceremony that became a dressing-room tradition during the 2023 ODI World Cup.The post-match award, introduced to celebrate exceptional fielding efforts, quickly evolved into one of the defining features of India's team culture, encouraging players to embrace athleticism and intensity in the field."The fielding medal will always hold a very special place in my heart. Seeing the excitement it created in the dressing room, the smiles it brought and the value the players attached to it are memories I'll carry with me forever," he wrote.Dilip also reflected on the team's glittering achievements during his tenure, saying he would always cherish being part of two T20 World Cup triumphs in 2024 and 2026, the Champions Trophy victory in 2025, Asia Cup titles in 2023 and 2025, as well as runner-up finishes in the 2023 ODI World Cup and World Test Championship.He thanked the BCCI for trusting him with the role and expressed gratitude to former head coach Rahul Dravid and current head coach Gautam Gambhir for their unwavering support.Dilip also acknowledged the captains he worked alongside over the years, including Rohit Sharma, Suryakumar Yadav, Virat Kohli, Hardik Pandya, Shubman Gill and Shreyas Iyer."To every player, coach and member of the support staff... thank you. The memories we've created together will stay with me for the rest of my life. As this chapter comes to a close, I'll always be grateful that, for five unforgettable years, I had the honour of wearing the India badge.Forever grateful. The journey continues," he concluded. Former India captain Rohit Sharma was among the first to pay tribute to Dilip , highlighting the enormous impact the coach had behind the scenes.Sharing a picture with Dilip on his Instagram story, Rohit wrote: "You are a legend Dillip guru. You created magic within the group and a behind the scenes workhorse. Best wishes ahead."The message summed up the respect Dilip earned within the dressing room, where he was widely credited with elevating India's fielding standards while fostering a competitive yet enjoyable atmosphere. His innovative medal ceremony became symbolic of that culture, with players such as Rohit Sharma, Virat Kohli, KL Rahul and Ravindra Jadeja among the notable recipients over the years.
Article Summary: T Dilip has left his role as India's fielding coach after five years. The Hyderabad-based coach left after his contract was not renewed. Subhadeep Ghosh has replaced him as the fielding coach and will travel with the team for the upcoming two-Test series against Sri Lanka.

MUMBAI: Jammu and Kashmir swing bowler Auqib Nabi was finally rewarded for his consistent performances in domestic cricket on Monday, being named the replacement for the injured Jasprit Bumrah in India’s Test squad for the two-match series in Sri Lanka.The 29-year-old has earned his maiden India call-up and if he makes his Test debut, will become the first cricketer from J&K to play a Test match for India.It marks a remarkable rise for the Baramulla seamer, who did not even own a pair of bowling spikes when he attended his first under-19 trials and had to borrow them from a friend.Nabi has taken a staggering 104 wickets across the last two Ranji Trophy seasons, including 60 at an astonishing average of 12.56 in the 2025-26 campaign, when he played a pivotal role in J&K’s maiden Ranji Trophy triumph. He also impressed on the recent India ‘A’ tour of Sri Lanka, claiming six wickets in two fourday matches, including figures of 4-58 in the first innings of the opening game.Named player of the tournament in the Ranji Trophy, Nabi registered seven five-wicket hauls last season. His standout performances included 5-54 in the final against Karnataka, match figures of 9-123 in the semifinal against Bengal and 12-110 in the quarterfinal against Madhya Pradesh.Former India allrounder Irfan Pathan believes Nabi has thoroughly earned his opportunity.“It’s not just about last season. Nabi has been performing consistently for a while now and I’m confident he’ll do well if he gets an opportunity. Sri Lanka usually offers seamers a bit of assistance, especially in humid conditions,” Pathan told TOI.Pathan also welcomed the selectors rewarding domestic performers such as Nabi and Madhya Pradesh off-spinning allrounder Saransh Jain. “It’s recognition for domestic cricket. Test cricket should reward consistent performances in the Ranji Trophy and Duleep Trophy,” he said.Having mentored J& K during his coaching stint, Pathan explained what makes Nabi so effective.“His action is compact and repeatable, allowing him to hit the seam consistently,” Pathan said. “His biggest strength is his seam position. Because it’s so upright, the ball moves late after pitching and forces batters to play. That’s why he has troubled even top domestic batters.”Pathan also believes Nabi’s experience of bowling long spells in first-class cricket will ease his transition to Test cricket. “He bowls long spells regularly, so his body is used to that workload. That’s a big advantage. Now it’s about making the most of the opportunity.” To those questioning Nabi’s pace, Pathan offered a blunt response. “How much pace do you want? If you’re dismissing batters while bowling in the 130s by making them play defensively, you’re doing something right.Control and late movement are what matter.”Former India allrounder Parvez Rasool, the first cricketer from J& K to represent India in international cricket, congratulated Nabi on social media. “What is meant for you will find you. No amount of rejection or ignorance can change your destiny. Heartiest congratulations, Auqib Nabi, on your well-deserved selection to the Indian Test squad.”
Article Summary: Auqib Nabi named in India's Test squad for two-match series in Sri Lanka. The 29-year-old will become the first cricketer from J&K to play a Test match for India. Former India allrounder Irfan Pathan believes Nabi has thoroughly earned his opportunity.

Former Indian umpire Anil Chaudhary has reflected on Virat Kohli 's fiery on-field personality, recalling the Royal Challengers Bengaluru (RCB) star's infamous altercation with Gautam Gambhir during the 2013 Indian Premier League ( IPL ). While praising Kohli's passion and intensity, Chaudhary stressed that aggression is an essential part of cricket, provided it does not cross the line.Speaking on JioHotstar, Chaudhary, who has officiated Kohli's matches since his junior cricket days in Delhi, said the former India captain has always been an emotional cricketer but never carries ill intent.Chaudhary revealed that his long association with Kohli helped him understand the batter's personality beyond his aggressive on-field image."Actually, my advantage with Virat was that I had officiated his matches since childhood, so I have known him for a long time. Between overs, he'll come over and put a hand around your waist. But he is lively throughout. Players like him should be there; otherwise, the game will get boring," he added.The veteran umpire also looked back at the much-talked-about confrontation between Kohli and Gautam Gambhir during an IPL 2013 clash between Royal Challengers Bengaluru and Kolkata Knight Riders. According to Chaudhary, such incidents were not entirely unexpected given the competitive nature of players from northern India."I knew something like that would happen because all of them from the North play with aggression. Article Title: 'A coterie hijacked him': Report claims Pakistan federation distanced itself from Arshad Nadeem before CWG flop
Article Text:
Pakistan's Arshad Nadeem (PTI Photo)

Federation 'distanced itself' from Olympic champion's preparations

Coach admits Nadeem was underprepared

Pakistan sporting structure under scrutiny

'A coterie hijacked him': Mentors question Nadeem's preparation

Pakistan's Olympic champion Arshad Nadeem has found himself at the centre of growing criticism following his disappointing Commonwealth Games campaign in Glasgow, with questions now being raised not just about his form but also about the support system that surrounded him in the lead-up to the competition.The defending Commonwealth Games champion endured one of the worst outings of his career, finishing ninth after failing to produce a throw beyond 80 metres. Sri Lanka's Rumesh Pathirage clinched the gold medal, while India's Neeraj Chopra and Yashvir Singh completed a historic South Asian podium with silver and bronze respectively.But as scrutiny intensified over Nadeem's performance, reports from Pakistan suggested the Olympic champion had effectively been left to prepare on his own after the Pakistan Amateur Athletics Federation (PAAF) allegedly distanced itself from his training programme following a dispute over the retention of his long-time coach Salman Butt According to a PTI report, the PAAF largely withdrew support from the star javelin thrower after disagreements emerged last year over his coaching setup. The report claimed that several requests made by Nadeem regarding his training programme were not entertained, while the Pakistan Sports Board also did not release funds to facilitate foreign coaches or trainers.Instead of training overseas under renowned South African coach Terseus Liebenberg, who had guided him before his Olympic triumph, Nadeem spent his Commonwealth Games build-up in Lahore with Salman Butt and local trainers.The contrast with India's preparation was striking. While Neeraj Chopra completed his final rehabilitation and training block in Biel, Switzerland, fellow Indian javelin throwers Yashvir Singh and Rohit Yadav trained in Spala, Poland, alongside foreign coaches and support staff before heading to Glasgow.The differing approaches were reflected in the final standings as India secured two medals, while Nadeem failed to qualify among the top eight after the opening three rounds.Nadeem had arrived in Glasgow with limited competitive exposure, having competed in only one preparatory meet in Switzerland during 2026. He also trained almost exclusively in Lahore despite the vastly different weather conditions between Pakistan and Scotland.His long-time coach Salman Butt admitted the Olympic champion was far from his best and acknowledged he was underprepared for the Games.Former Pakistan Athletics Federation president Akram Sahi also blamed negligence and inadequate preparation for the dramatic decline."Since Nadeem's Olympic gold medal a coterie has hijacked him and never let him come to me," Sahi told Telecom Asia Sport."This result in Glasgow is hugely disappointing... the signs were imminent for the last several months as there was negligence and lack of training."Another mentor, speaking anonymously, argued that Nadeem had become complacent and failed to invest sufficiently in elite overseas training after receiving substantial financial rewards following his Olympic success.Nadeem's disappointing campaign has reignited debate over Pakistan's sporting ecosystem.Former Olympic boxing bronze medallist Hussain Shah described the situation as a reflection of systemic shortcomings."This is an athlete who is self-made and comes from a village and belongs to a low-income family. But he brought so much glory to Pakistan with his gold medals. And yet he couldn't prepare properly for the CWG. It is a sad reflection on our sports structure," Shah said.Pakistan's campaign in Glasgow also exposed wider concerns. Boxer Fatima Zehra, who secured the country's only medal with bronze, also lamented the lack of quality preparation and international exposure, saying better training could have helped her challenge for gold.The criticism did not stop with Pakistan's athletics authorities. Two of Nadeem's former mentors also questioned the Olympic champion's preparation, alleging that a lack of quality training and poor decisions contributed to his disappointing campaign.Akram Sahi, the former Pakistan Athletics Federation president who helped identify Nadeem's talent in 2018, claimed the warning signs had been visible for months."Since Nadeem's Olympic gold medal a coterie has hijacked him and never let him come to me," Sahi told Telecom Asia Sport."This result in Glasgow is hugely disappointing for someone who has risen to new heights, but the signs were imminent for the last several months as there was negligence and lack of training."Another mentor, speaking anonymously, echoed those concerns, suggesting Nadeem had not trained adequately after returning from Haj and had become overly dependent on official support."He won the Olympics after he got extensive training from his South African coach Terseus Liebenberg. His training stints at Northwest University Potchefstroom also helped him clinch Olympic gold. Now he waited for the federation and government to send him to South Africa for training.He should have invested in himself rather than waiting for someone else," the mentor said.The mentor also questioned Nadeem's current coaching setup, claiming his long-time coach Salman Butt lacked specialist expertise in javelin and that the Olympic champion had become distracted by business ventures after receiving substantial financial rewards following his Paris triumph.
Article Summary: Pakistan's Olympic champion Arshad Nadeem finished ninth in the javelin throw at the Commonwealth Games in Glasgow. Reports suggest the Pakistan Amateur Athletics Federation (PAAF) 'distanced itself' from his training programme following a dispute over the retention of his long-time coach Salman Butt. Former Pakistan Athletics Federation president Akram Sahi blamed negligence and inadequate preparation for the dramatic decline. Former Olympic boxing bronze medallist Hussain Shah described the situation as a reflection of systemic shortcomings.

Chris Bosh's health scare in January was more serious than fans realized. The Miami Heat legend revealed he suffered a second pulmonary embolism that nearly killed him, landing him in the hospital for a week and forcing him to relive a fight he thought he had already beaten.The revelation, shared in an interview with Hoops Hype, comes months after Bosh first opened up about waking up covered in his own blood. Now the 11-time All-Star details how close that moment came to being fatal, and why he's urging Victor Wembanyama to stay disciplined in his recovery.Bosh told Hoops Hype the scare unfolded without warning. He suffered another pulmonary embolism in January, his second brush with a life-threatening blood clot since his playing days ended, and spent a week in the hospital recovering. He said no symptoms appeared beforehand, a detail that shook him as much as the emergency itself.The Hall of Famer had previously described the incident in a February social media post, writing that he woke up covered in blood after collapsing at home. He said the experience brought no dramatic realization or flash of clarity, just a deep sense of gratitude for still being alive and a simpler, more honest way of approaching each day since.Bosh explained the scare reinforced a lesson he thought he'd already learned. He assumed his fight with blood clots was behind him, only to discover the condition can resurface without notice, which is why he now treats his daily medication and monitoring as non-negotiable for the rest of his life.Bosh used the moment to speak directly to Victor Wembanyama, the Spurs star whose season was interrupted by a blood clot of his own. His message was simple: stay consistent with treatment, because it only takes one more slip for the situation to turn permanent, something Bosh knows firsthand after his own career ended that way.Wembanyama returned to action, playing 64 games and reportedly helping the Spurs reach the Western Conference championship and a trip to the NBA Finals, while also earning Defensive Player of the Year and an MVP finalist nod. Bosh's warning is a reminder that the danger doesn't disappear once the symptoms do.Bosh spent 13 seasons in the league before blood clots forced his retirement in 2019. He now manages the condition daily, a routine he says he can never afford to skip again.

Article Title: What’s going on with Tony Romo? Greg Olsen’s name floats as successor despite $72 million remaining contract
Article Text:

What's going on with NFL analyst Tony Romo at CBS?

Tony Romo. Image via: Getty Images

Greg Olsen could be Tony Romo's successor

Greg Olsen. Image via: Brian Westerholt/ AP

3 potential landing spots for Tony Romo

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Tony Romo's future at CBS is suddenly in question after the network announced Friday that its lead NFL analyst would step away "until further notice" following an OWI arrest in Wisconsin. J.J. Watt, CBS's No. 2 analyst, has already moved into the top booth alongside Jim Nantz.The speed of that shift has fueled speculation that CBS sees more than a temporary fix. With $72 million still owed to Romo, the network faces a costly choice between paying him out, settling, or fighting to terminate the deal for cause.Tony Romo signed a 10-year, $18-million-a-year deal with CBS in 2020, a contract that reset the market for top NFL analysts. Four years remain, worth $72 million total. CBS could attempt to terminate the deal for cause and owe Romo nothing, but that route risks a legal fight. A settlement, potentially around $36 million, is seen as the more realistic outcome if the split becomes permanent.Watt's rapid promotion has led some media observers to read the move as more than a stopgap. Whether Romo's absence proves temporary or permanent now hinges largely on how CBS wants to handle both his contract and its own broadcast product going forward.According to John Ourand's Varsity newsletter for Puck, Watt and Greg Olsen stand out as the two names CBS could turn to long-term if it moves on from Romo. Olsen has the flexibility to leave his current Fox deal if offered a top analyst chair elsewhere, having already lost Fox's lead role to Tom Brady.Olsen's résumé backs up the buzz. He has won three Emmys, and he beat out Brady for Outstanding Personality/Event Analyst earlier this year. That combination of availability and pedigree makes him one of the most logical candidates if CBS decides Watt alone isn't the long-term answer.Netflix is building out its NFL package through the 2029-30 season, airing four marquee games a year. The streamer has so far leaned on borrowed or lower-profile talent, including Luke Kuechly for its Week 1 broadcast. A name like Romo's would immediately raise the profile of those broadcasts.Prime Video's Thursday Night Football booth may open up soon, with Al Michaels, 81, on a year-to-year deal and Kirk Herbstreit's contract expiring after this season. Romo would face competition for the job, notably from Olsen, who has long been linked to it.Fox's studio show is another plausible fit. Fox airs more Cowboys games than any other network, and 77-year-old Terry Bradshaw won't anchor the panel forever. Romo would slot naturally into the network's history of star-power studio panelists.Cowboys owner Jerry Jones has already made his position known. "I love him. I love what he's about. I love his character," Jones said, adding that Romo's ability to handle adversity has defined his career on and off the field. Jones's influence around the league could become a real factor if CBS moves toward a permanent break, turning Romo's situation into as much a power question as a broadcasting one.
Article Summary: Tony Romo signed a 10-year, $18-million-a-year deal with CBS in 2020. J.J. Watt and Greg Olsen stand out as the two names CBS could turn to long-term if it moves on from Romo. Prime Video's Thursday Night Football booth may open up soon.

International Cricket Council (ICC) Chairman Jay Shah on Sunday inaugurated the Tanzania Cricket Arena (TCA Arena) in Dar es Salaam, marking a historic milestone for the country's cricketing journey. The venue is the first-ever ICC-approved cricket stadium in Tanzania and is expected to play a pivotal role in developing the sport across East Africa.The inauguration also marks the first time an ICC Chairman has visited Tanzania to officially open a cricket venue, underlining the ICC's commitment to expanding the game's footprint beyond traditional cricketing nations.Located at the University of Dar es Salaam (UDSM), the TCA Arena has been built as Tanzania's permanent home for cricket. The modern facility comprises two international-standard cricket ovals and will serve as the country's national high-performance centre.The venue will be used for:The project moved swiftly from conception to completion. Land for the stadium was allocated in October 2024, construction began after the groundbreaking ceremony in April 2025, and the facility was completed in July 2026.The newly inaugurated venue is set to stage its first major international tournament when it hosts the ICC Men's Cricket World Cup Challenge League B from August 8 to August 18, 2026.The tournament is a key qualification pathway towards the ICC Men's Cricket World Cup, making Tanzania's debut as a host nation a significant moment for cricket in the region.The inauguration ceremony was attended by Tanzania Cricket Association (TCA) Chairman Dr B.S. Sreekumar, ICC delegates, and senior government officials.Speaking at the inauguration, ICC Chairman Jay Shah praised the Tanzania Cricket Association for its vision and commitment to growing the sport."The inauguration of the TCA Arena is a significant milestone for cricket in Tanzania and demonstrates what can be achieved through vision, commitment and strong collaboration. The progress made by the Tanzania Cricket Association is remarkable. TCA have shown great ambition and determination in developing a modern cricket facility while continuing to expand participation, strengthen its workforce and create better opportunities for players across the country, '' Jay Shah said."The TCA Arena represents an exciting future for cricket in Tanzania and the wider African region. It will provide an important platform for Tanzania to host international cricket, develop its players, coaches and match officials, and inspire more young people to become involved in the game. The ICC will continue to work alongside Tanzania and its other Members to enhance cricket infrastructure, build local capability and ensure that the opportunities available through ICC programmes are used to create sustainable growth," he added.Tanzania Cricket Association Chairman Dr B.S. Sreekumar described the inauguration as a landmark occasion for the country's sporting landscape."The inauguration of the TCA Arena is a defining moment for cricket in Tanzania. This facility is far more than a cricket ground; it represents a vision for the future of our sport and demonstrates what can be achieved through strong partnerships, commitment and belief. We are proud to provide our players, coaches and future generations with a world-class home for cricket, while creating new opportunities to host international competitions and inspire more young Tanzanians to embrace the game, " Dr B.S. Sreekumar, Tanzania Cricket Association Chairman, said.
Article Summary: The Tanzania Cricket Arena is the first-ever ICC-approved cricket stadium in Tanzania. The venue is expected to play a pivotal role in developing the sport across East Africa. The newly inaugurated venue is set to stage its first major international tournament when it hosts the ICC Men's Cricket World Cup Challenge League B in 2026.

Article Title: After England retirement, Ben Stokes tipped for record AUD 600K BBL comeback

Former England captain Ben Stokes. (Photo by Gareth Copley/Getty Images)

Stokes keen to continue playing after international retirement



Record-breaking BBL contract on the cards

Former England Test captain Ben Stokes could become the highest-paid player in Big Bash League (BBL) history after retiring from international cricket after series defeat against New Zeland. According to reports from Code Sports, the all-rounder is attracting significant interest from multiple BBL franchises, with the Sydney Sixers leading the race for his signature ahead of the 2026/27 season.Stokes announced his retirement from international cricket in June 2026, bringing the curtain down on a glittering England career. However, the 35-year-old has made it clear that he has no plans to step away from the game entirely and intends to continue playing domestic and franchise cricket around the world.Unlike several former international captains who moved directly into coaching or broadcasting, Stokes wants to remain an active cricketer. The England great recently returned to action for Durham and is expected to play a larger role in the County Championship, hoping to help his home county achieve sustained success.Now, as per Code Sports, Ben Stokes has shown interest for BBL and a bidding war has reportedly broken out among BBL franchises, with the Sydney Sixers emerging as the frontrunners to secure Stokes' services.The Sixers' advantage stems from the appointment of former England white-ball coach Matthew Mott, who shares a successful history with Stokes. The pair famously guided England to the 2022 T20 World Cup title in Australia, with Stokes scoring an unbeaten 52 in the final against Pakistan at the Melbourne Cricket Ground.Stokes is also no stranger to the Big Bash, having represented the Melbourne Renegades during the 2014/15 season. However, several other franchises are also monitoring the situation closely. The Hobart Hurricanes are among the teams interested, with Cricket Tasmania previously expressing its desire to bring the England star to Tasmania.Reports suggest Cricket Australia is optimistic about securing Stokes for at least part of the upcoming BBL season. The proposed marquee deal is believed to be worth around AUD 600,000, which could make Stokes the most expensive overseas signing in BBL history.One challenge remains scheduling. Stokes may prefer to spend Christmas with his family in England before potentially joining another franchise competition. The South Africa-based SA20 begins in January, creating a possible scheduling conflict for the all-rounder.n immediate IPL return, however, appears unlikely. Under current BCCI regulations, Stokes cannot enter the IPL auction until 2028 after opting out of the 2025 mega auction. Players who skip the mega auction are ineligible for the subsequent mini auctions under the existing rules. He is also unavailable for the current edition of The Hundred, having not registered for the player draft.

The Sydney Sixers are leading the race for his signature ahead of the 2026/27 season. Stokes announced his retirement from international cricket in June 2026.

Does your mother still insist that studies come first?

Consistency is often the hardest quality to master in domestic cricket. Smaran Ravichandran has done exactly that. With 1534 runs in 26 innings at an average of 73.60, including three double hundreds in the last two Ranji Trophy seasons, the Karnataka batter has firmly established himself as one of the brightest young talents in the country and has shown that he is far from a one-season wonder.More importantly, Smaran has shown the versatility to excel across formats, seamlessly adapting his tempo to the demands of the game. He was the driving force behind Karnataka's 2024-25 Vijay Hazare Trophy triumph, ending the state's five-year wait for a major title. Smaran piled up 433 runs in seven innings at an average of 72.16, including two centuries and two fifties. In the Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy, he finished as Karnataka's leading run-scorer with 319 runs in seven innings, averaging 63.80 at a strike rate of 160.With back-to-back stellar seasons behind him, Smaran now has his sights set on the next step. In an exclusive conversation with TimesofIndia.com, the left-hander speaks about his India dream, the disappointment of missing out on the latest India A squad, his leadership ambitions, the art of succeeding across formats, and why his mother still refuses to let him ignore the value of education.ExcerptsI'm 100% fit now. The recovery has gone really well and I'm ready to play again.Missing the Emerging Teams tournament was heartbreaking because every opportunity matters. But there are plenty of things to look forward to this season. Right now, I'm fully fit and excited to get back on the field.Preparation becomes extremely important, especially during the off-season. A lot of credit goes to Syed (Zabiulla) Sir because he plans my training in a way that simulates the challenges I'll face during the Ranji Trophy. We train on different kinds of wickets, including red-soil and black-soil surfaces, and we deliberately practise on difficult pitches. Batting on flat wickets is comparatively easier because most batters can adjust, but scoring on challenging wickets requires a different level of preparation.In India, wickets tend to assist spin as the game progresses into the third and fourth days. So batting on those surfaces during practice is very important. It prepares you not only for the first innings but also for the second innings when conditions become tougher. Batting against different bowlers in different conditions has helped me overcome many challenges that come during matches.At times, he is very demanding, especially when it comes to discipline and following the process. He believes in completing every small task because those little things help you grow both as a cricketer and as a person.From my childhood, discipline and commitment to the game have always come first. As I grew older, he eased up a little, but his core values haven't changed. He still ensures that every practice session has purpose and quality because that's what ultimately helps you improve.Again, it comes back to off-season preparation. During training, I constantly switch formats. For example, I might spend two days batting with the red ball and then move straight to white-ball practice. Doing this repeatedly over four to six weeks helps your muscle memory and instincts adapt naturally.Switching from red-ball to white-ball cricket is comparatively easier because you're adding more scoring options. But moving back from white-ball to red-ball cricket can be challenging because you have to leave more deliveries and be patient outside off stump. I feel the off-season training helps my body and mind make those transitions smoothly.Not really. For me, it's more about mindset than technique. The red ball swings for longer and demands greater patience. You have to respect good spells and understand that you're batting for long periods to build an innings. As long as I'm in the right headspace and understand the match situation, I don't feel the need to change my technique.I definitely think it's possible. Playing in the V can still be effective, but you also need to develop a wider range of shots because bowlers constantly vary their pace and lengths in T20 cricket.It doesn't necessarily mean playing scoops or other unconventional shots, but you need enough options to make the bowler uncomfortable and force him to bowl where you want him to. Nowadays, teams are scoring and chasing 240 or even 250. To contribute consistently in that environment, you have to broaden your scoring areas while continuing to trust your natural strengths.Playing spin becomes increasingly important as you move up the levels, especially in the subcontinent, where pitches often assist spin more than seam. I feel the sweep and reverse sweep are very important because they force the spinner to change his lengths and lines.You can always rely on your defence, but if you want to score consistently and dominate quality spin bowling, you need those additional options.That's something I'm working on this season. Even if I don't use those shots on every wicket, it's important to have them in my game for turning tracks.Sunrisers Hyderabad have been fantastic as a franchise. They've always backed their players and created a very supportive environment. Sharing a dressing room with players like Ishan Kishan, Abhishek Sharma, Heinrich Klaasen and Travis Head was a huge learning experience. Watching how they prepare, practise and approach T20 cricket teaches you a lot.Coming into the IPL, I had scored plenty of runs in domestic cricket and I was confident. But that's the nature of the game. You don't score runs everywhere you go. It was a valuable learning experience. Last year I couldn't play because of the injury, so I was grateful to get six matches this season.Things didn't go according to plan, but I now know the areas I need to improve. The off-season gives me an opportunity to work on those aspects so that I'm better prepared for the next IPL and can contribute much more to the team.Definitely. I've always enjoyed leading teams. It's a privilege, and there's no better feeling than winning a championship as captain.I've captained Karnataka at the age-group level and we won the CK Nayudu Trophy. More recently, I was part of the Maharaja Trophy-winning side as well. Leadership is something I've always looked forward to, so if that opportunity comes, it would be a great honour.I knew the series was coming and naturally I was hoping to be part of the squad.Of course, I felt I had a chance, but I didn't dwell on it for too long. My focus immediately shifted towards scoring even more runs this season.Every year there's a different leading run-scorer in the Ranji Trophy. My goal is to remain at the top and continue piling on runs. Ultimately, your bat has to do the talking. India has so many quality cricketers that the only thing within your control is your performance. If I keep scoring consistently, opportunities will eventually come.Yes, ideally I would. I've always batted at No. 4. Last season, Karun Nair was batting there and both of us were scoring runs, so we didn't want to disturb a combination that was working well. If the opportunity comes, I'd love to bat in the top four. Whether that's No. 3 or No. 4 doesn't really matter.At the same time, my priority is helping Karnataka win championships. If batting at No. 5 gives the team the best chance of winning, I'm happy to do that as well.Sachin Tendulkar has been an inspiration to every cricketer growing up, but my number isn't because of him. I used to wear No. 5. One day my mother suggested that I switch to No. 10. I did, and I've never changed it since.My family has been incredibly supportive throughout my life.It was actually my mother who enrolled me in cricket coaching because I was a very naughty child. Syed Sir happened to coach at the ground near our home, and that's where everything started. My family comes from an academic background. Most of them are engineers, so cricket was something completely new for them. Even then, they never pressured me.The emphasis was always on balancing studies and cricket. My mother always ensured I did well in school and college while pursuing cricket seriously.Whenever I come home, they support me regardless of whether I've scored runs or not. My mother may ask what went wrong after a poor innings, but that's simply a mother's concern.Syed Sir has also been like family. He wasn't just my coach; he played a big role in convincing my parents to let me pursue cricket seriously. I also have an elder sister, who is six years older than me. She doesn't follow cricket closely but she always watches my IPL matches and sends me a message whenever I do well.I'm fortunate to have such a supportive family around me.(Laughs) Yes, absolutely. That's probably the conversation we have the most. She always reminds me that I should have a good educational background and a career beyond cricket.She believes studies are just as important, and I completely respect her viewpoint. Even today, I feel education and cricket should go hand-in-hand because balancing both teaches you a lot about discipline and life. Credit goes entirely to my family for helping me maintain that balance.
Article Summary: Smaran Ravichandran has delivered back-to-back outstanding Ranji Trophy seasons. He was the driving force behind Karnataka's 2024-25 Vijay Hazare Trophy triumph. Smaran has shown the versatility to excel across formats.

Article Title: 'You are a fool to live so openly, Mallya told Nirav before his arrest'
Article Text:
TOI correspondent from London

: Economic fugitive Vijay Mallya invited fellow billionaire Nirav Modi to his multi-million-pound townhouse overlooking Regent's Park where the pair discussed their respective exiles when the latter was living freely in London before his arrest, the final podcast of the "Diamond King", released Friday, claims.A source in the diamond trade who tipped off Telegraph about Nirav's location, leading to his arrest in March 2019, claims in Episode 4: "Mallya and Nirav were in contact... But Nirav did not get bail and has been in a London jail for seven years.Despite an Interpol red notice, Nirav "would regularly stop for a cup of coffee at a cafe in Oxford Street where he would sit reading newspapers... where anyone could see him," the source said. However, he started taking precautions later. To avoid being seen in restaurants, he would pay private chefs £200 to £300 per hour to come to his apartment and cook, but they were never of Indian origin, and it was never the same chef twice, the podcast revealed."I don't think he was clever enough to come up with the (Punjab National Bank) scam himself," the source added. The podcast speculates that Nirav has submitted a second asylum case, which is why he has not gone back. Nirav's solicitor Anand Doobay, who Mallya also used, told TOI: "We are not commenting."

El Rubius reflects on a tough and “unfair” exit

Article Title: Clavicular Viral Controversy: "Trans women are.....": Clavicular’s viral moment with trans women sparks fresh conversation on internet culture

A viral clip featuring Clavicular and trans women is gaining attention for its calm and honest tone. The conversation explores how online language and trends move across communities. Clavicular and trans women share a surprising realization about online trends







The video of Clavicular, a short-video producer, is going around the Internet, yet not the reason why. There is no yelling or over-the-top drama. It is a mere, everyday talk that seems almost novel nowadays, in the age of internet, which is overflowing with content. It discusses internet culture, the way people communicate with one another and the place of trends. Rather than bringing out a debate, the encounter towards curiosity. It quietly brings attention to something that a lot of people who use the internet notice but don't often say out loud. Article Title: 'This is my final post': Shradha Singh posts emotional message after RAF controversy video at Jantar Mantar
Article Text:
Social media influencer Shradha Singh has posted her final statement regarding recent controversies





NEW DELHI: Social media influencer Shradha Singh, who came under intense online scrutiny after her viral video featuring Rapid Action Force (RAF) personnel and the subsequent controversy at the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP)-led protest at Jantar Mantar, has shared what she described as her "final post" on the episode, thanking supporters and saying she wants to move on.In a video posted on social media, Singh said she no longer wanted to prolong the controversy and hoped to "close this chapter"."This is my final post about everything that has happened," she wrote in the caption, adding that life was "too precious to stay stuck in one moment".Thanking those who supported her through the controversy, Singh said the positive comments and messages she received had helped her overcome the negativity.She said that while earlier she had to search for encouraging comments, she now saw them in abundance and that they had "covered up" the hateful remarks directed at her.Responding to criticism that she was "playing the victim card", Singh said she had even started controlling her emotions because people were mocking her for crying.She also said people continued to abuse and target her despite the fact that she had "not abused the Prime Minister, his mother or the Army."Referring to the viral RAF video, Singh said she had only made a video with the personnel and had later apologised for it.She also said the extensive media attention surrounding the controversy had amplified the situation, though she thanked sections of the media for helping her during the difficult period."I just want to say thank you to everyone who stood by me, understood me, and took the time to send kind comments and heartfelt DMs. Your love, prayers, and support gave me strength when I needed it the most," she wrote."Now, I truly want to close this chapter. I don't want this situation to continue any further. Life is too precious to stay stuck in one moment. Let's leave the past behind, move forward with kindness, and focus on better days ahead," the post added.The latest video comes weeks after Shradha found herself at the centre of a social media storm over a video with RAF personnel and amid the wider controversy surrounding the CJP-led NEET protest at Delhi's Jantar Mantar.She had earlier apologised over the RAF video and subsequently alleged that online trolling, memes and intense public scrutiny had taken a severe emotional toll on her.
