Article Title: They were brought back from brink. How are they doing now?
Article Text:
(AI image used for representative) Modern medicine offers new hope for patients with complex conditions

A second shot at childhood

A second shot at childhood

Rebuilding life after paralysis

Rebuilding life after paralysis

Tummy ache reveals rare disease

Tummy ache reveals rare disease

Breathing again after end-stage lung disease

Breathing again after end-stage lung disease





NEW DELHI:For a decade, a single mother from a Kerala village lived with one hope: that her daughter might one day live a life free of epileptic seizuresThe 12-year-old had battled drug-resistant epilepsy since suffering a severe stroke at the age of nine months. Born with congenital heart disease and dilated cardiomyopathy, she endured one to two seizures every day despite years of treatment. Conventional brain surgery was considered too risky because of her fragile heart.Determined to find a solution, her mother secured financial assistance through the Kerala chief minister's relief fund and travelled 2,500 km to AIIMS Delhi in April 2024.After evaluation, a multidisciplinary team led by Prof Manjari Tripathi, head of neurology, opted for robotic thermocoagulative hemispherotomy (ROTCH), an ultra-minimally invasive technique developed at AIIMS. Instead of opening the skull, the procedure disconnects the damaged half of the brain through tiny keyhole pathways, reducing blood loss and surgical trauma.The surgery took a dramatic turn when the girl suffered a cardiac arrest on the operating table. Doctors revived her after nearly 30 minutes before completing the operation.During follow-up, doctors detected a chronic subdural haematoma, a complication that usually requires open brain surgery.Given her fragile heart, Prof Ajay Garg and his neuroradiology team performed a middle meningeal artery embolisation, a minimally invasive procedure that sealed the bleeding vessel and avoided another major surgery.She had been seizure free till 2 years of follow up."Earlier, it was tough for her to sit through classes. Now, she feels much better and can lead a normal life," her mother told TOI.Prof P Sarat Chandra, who lead the team along with Prof Ramesh Doddamani, said the case demonstrated what was possible when innovation was combined with multidisciplinary teamwork.Few procedures test the limits of neurosurgery like removing a recurrent spinal tumour that has destroyed a vertebra, invaded the chest cavity and left a patient paralysed.That was the challenge before the neurosurgery team at PSRI Hospital, Delhi, when Kiran Kumar Chetri (40) was admitted in February after undergoing two previous surgeries in Sikkim.His tumour had returned aggressively, growing to the size of a tennis ball, destroying a lower thoracic vertebra, compressing the spinal cord and breaching the chest cavity, causing a haemothorax. Within days, he lost movement in both legs and complete bladder and bowel control. The distorted anatomy, previous implants and collapsed spine made another surgery exceptionally risky.A team led by Dr Amitabh Gupta, director of neurosurgery, planned a staged operation involving rib resection, entry into the thoracic cavity, drainage of accumulated blood, and removal of the tumour from both inside and outside the spinal canal. The most delicate step involved freeing the spinal cord, which had been completely encased by the tumour. Once the tumour was removed, surgeons reconstructed and stabilised the collapsed spine.The outcome exceeded expectations for a patient destined for a life of paralysis. Gradually, Chetri regained movement in his legs, bladder control, bowel function and began rehabilitation."The outcome of operating on recurrent spinal tumours is never guaranteed because each surgery becomes progressively more complex," Dr Gupta said, attributing Chetri's recovery to meticulous planning, advanced imaging and coordinated multidisciplinary care."We can't imagine he is walking again," Chetri's guardian, Milan Subba, said, adding that the Sikkim government paid Rs 7.4 lakh for the treatment.A stomach ache is one of the most common complaints. For doctors at Fortis Escorts Hospital, Okhla, however, one seemingly routine case proved that common symptoms can sometimes conceal extraordinary illnesses requiring innovative treatment.In April 2025, a 61-year-old man walked in with severe abdominal pain that had persisted for two weeks. He had no fever, vomiting, diarrhoea or intestinal bleeding, leaving doctors with few obvious clues. The first breakthrough came after blood tests showed a markedly elevated eosinophil count — white blood cells usually linked to allergies or parasitic infections.Specialists launched an exhaustive search, investigating parasites, food allergies, inflammatory bowel disease and eosinophilic gastroenteritis. Every test ruled out the expected diagnoses.An endoscopy then revealed multiple ulcers throughout the intestines, while biopsies showed dense eosinophilic infiltration, suggesting the immune system itself was attacking the digestive tract.The mystery deepened when a routine cardiac evaluation detected subtle ECG changes and elevated cardiac enzymes. Although a coronary angiography ruled out blocked arteries, a cardiac MRI revealed inflammation of the heart muscle. Soon afterwards, the patient developed numbness in one leg, with nerve conduction studies confirming peripheral nerve damage.Viewed individually, none of these findings pointed conclusively to a diagnosis. Together, however, they painted the picture of eosinophilic granulomatosis with polyangiitis (EGPA), formerly known as Churg-Strauss syndrome — a rare autoimmune disorder in which the immune system attacks small blood vessels across multiple organs.The diagnosis was especially challenging because the patient's ANCA blood test, commonly used to detect EGPA, was negative. High-dose steroid therapy was started, resulting in a dramatic recovery. The abdominal pain subsided rapidly, his condition stabilised, and he was soon back on his feet."We diagnosed a rare case of abdominal pain caused by an autoimmune disease that is extremely rare, affecting around one in a million people. On top of that, the disease presenting as abdominal pain is even rarer," said Dr Shubham Prasad, consultant gastroenterologist.A year ago, the world of a 65-year-old woman from Faridabad had narrowed to the length of an oxygen tube. Speaking for just a few minutes left her breathless. Diagnosed with end-stage interstitial lung disease caused by scleroderma, a rare autoimmune condition that progressively scars the lungs, she relied on five litres of oxygen every minute. Even daily activities such as bathing and walking had become exhausting.Today, she can breathe independently. Her recovery follows a successful bilateral lung transplant at Indraprastha Apollo Hospital, marking an important milestone for lung transplantation in north India — a procedure that had previously been successfully performed only once in the region, at AIIMS.Suitable donor lungs are among the scarcest organs available for transplantation because only a fraction of donated lungs meets the criteria for transplant.There was a glimmer of hope for the woman when the family of a 48-year-old man from Noida consented to organ donation after he was declared brain dead.The seven-hour transplant required extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) support, a life-support system that temporarily performs the functions of the heart and lungs. This was followed by months of intensive rehabilitation before the transplanted lungs fully adapted.The patient has now resumed an independent life."Earlier, I found it impossible to carry out even simple activities. Now, I feel energetic and can step outside again," she said."Completing one year after a bilateral lung transplant is a significant milestone," said Dr Avdhesh Bansal, senior consultant, respiratory medicine.According to Dr Mukesh Goel, senior consultant, cardiothoracic surgery, the achievement signals a broader shift in regional healthcare."Patients from north India once had to travel to Chennai or Hyderabad for such specialised care. Not anymore," he said.
Article Summary: Kiran Kumar Chetri, 40, was admitted in February after undergoing two previous surgeries in Sikkim. His tumour had returned aggressively, growing to the size of a tennis ball, destroying a lower thoracic vertebra, compressing the spinal cord and breaching the chest cavity, causing a haemothorax. A team led by Dr Amitabh Gupta, director of neurosurgery, planned a staged operation involving rib resection, entry into the thorACic cavity and removal of the tumour.

Article Title: For some, LSR’s renovated hostel means more than just accommodation
Article Text:
New Delhi:





Lady Shri Ram College’s residence hall has reopened after four years of renovation, bringing 100 upgraded rooms back into use for around 150 students. the reopening has opened doors to students whose lives are shaped by financial hardship, disability and long commutes.The college, which receives around 700 hostel applications from first-year students each year, has also expanded accommodation for second- and third-year students with disabilities.Among them is second-year political science student Kafi Chaudhary, an acid attack survivor who spent her first year in a paying guest accommodation. Visually impaired after the attack, she said the move had eased her financial and emotional burden.When Kafi walked into her hostel room this week, it was “Ia huge relief financially. Beyond that, the hostel facilities are far better than what I had in a paying guest accommodation,” she said.Now, settled into her room, Kafi can focus on pursuing her long-held dream of becoming an IAS officer. “It feels great. The food is almost like home, and the facilities are really good. What stands out is how accessible the hostel is for persons with disabilities.There are ramps throughout the building, and room numbers are in Braille,” she said.Her journey to Delhi University has been marked by extraordinary resilience. In 2011, during Holi celebrations, Kafi was attacked with acid when she was three years old. The assault left her blind and set her on a long road of medical treatment and reconstructive surgeries. “I underwent some treatment immediately after the attack, but the doctors told me that further reconstructive procedures could only be done after I turned 18. Now that I’m 18, I’ve undergone two minor surgeries this year, but it’s still a long journey ahead,” she said.Yet, neither the attack nor the years of treatment changed the future Kafi sees for herself. The dream she spoke about as a schoolgirl -- to study at Delhi University and one day become an IAS officer -- remained intact.The journey, however, has been about more than rebuilding her physical health. . “I wasn’t able to interact much because I had this inferiority complex. There were incidents where people screamed after seeing me,” she said.Delhi University helped change that perception. She found a campus where students were more aware of disability and more accepting than she had expected, she said.LSR principal Kanika K Ahuja said the reopening is significant not just because of the upgraded infrastructure. “The renovated hostel is much more than a building reopening. It means that many students from economically disadvantaged backgrounds, OBC, EWS and PwD categories now have a safe place to stay,” she said.She added, “Last year, Kafi wrote to me repeatedly asking for hostel accommodation. I even explored whether we could arrange for a place for her elsewhere, but it wasn’t possible. When we decided to open hostel admissions for second- and third-year PwD students, I immediately remembered her and asked that she be informed so she could apply. Today she has finally moved into the hostel, and seeing her so happy has been deeply satisfying,” Ahuja said.
Article Summary: Lady Shri Ram College’s residence hall has reopened after four years of renovation. The reopening has opened doors to students whose lives are shaped by financial hardship, disability and long commutes. Among them is second-year political science student Kafi Chaudhary, an acid attack survivor.

Article Title: 4 held for theft of 17 kg silver mask, cladding of Shivling at historic temple in Maharashtra's Khopoli
Article Text:
Khopoli police arrested four burglars for stealing silver items from a historic temple





NAVI MUMBAI: The Khopoli police in Raigad detected the burglary at the 18th century historic Shree Vireshwar temple, where 17 kg silver mask and silver cladding on Shivling was stolen on July 19 past midnight around 2 am, by arresting four accused burglars on Tuesday.The arrested accused are Amol Kasbe (36) and Vikas Agiwale (25), who were arrested from Shirur, Pune district and Dilip Jadhav (40) and Sakharam Gaikwad (40), who were arrested from Parner in Ahilyanagar district.The 17 kg silver mask and cladding on the Shivling was adorned in 2023 for which the around Rs 28 lakhs expenses were borne by the temple's trust from the donations received from devotees.Sachin Hire, senior inspector of Khopoli said, "On July 19, the assistant priest at the temple identified as Kishore Shigwan (56) lodge a complaint that the silver mask and cladding on Shivling was stolen. The thieves had entered the temple by breaking the chain and lock of the rear gate, which always remained close as the devotees were allowed entry only from the front gate.""Upon checking CCTV camera footage at the temple, it was seen that four masked men had entered the sanctum sanctorum around 2 am and decamped with the silver mask and cladding on the Shivling. Subsequently, an FIR was registered under BNS sections for house tres-pass, theft in a dwelling house and joint criminal liability. "Inspector Hire said, "Multiple teams were formed to trace the gang of burglars.Using technical expertise and informer network, we zeroed-in on four history-sheeters. They were traced to Pune and Ahilyanagar district and gradually apprehended on Tuesday.""They have revealed the place where they have hidden the stolen silver mask and cladding. Accordingly, a police team will recover the stolen valuables. Previously, there are criminal cases of theft and robbery registered against the arrested accused in Ahilyanagar and Pune districts."
Article Summary: The 17 kg silver mask and cladding on the Shivling was adorned in 2023 for which the around Rs 28 lakhs expenses were borne by the temple's trust. The arrested accused are Amol Kasbe, Vikas Agiwale, Dilip Jadhav and Sakharam Gaikwad.

Article Title: Man booked for sexually assaulting and injuring stray dog in Navi Mumbai
Article Text:
Unidentified man booked for sexually assaulting female stray dog (Representative image generated using AI)





NAVI MUMBAI: A 31-year-old woman advocate, who is a dog lover, has registered an FIR at Ulwe police station against an unidentified man aged 30-35 years for allegedly sexually assaulting a female stray dog and causing injury to her private part.The incident occurred outside a tea shop on the ground floor in Siddhivinayak Platinum society in sector 23, Ulwe on Sunday around 11.45pm.Acting on a complaint by Advocate Gayatri Khanvilkar, a resident of the said building, the unidentified accused was booked under BNS section and Prevention of Cruelty to Animal.Adv Khanvilkar said, "As per my daily routine, on Sunday night, I went downstairs to feed the stray dogs loitering near our building. It was raining heavily and pitch darkness due to defunct streetlight poles.""I pucker whistled to call the dogs, when a female stray dog, who had delivered puppies last month, came out from behind a plastic table kept horizontally lying on the floor outside the closed tea shop next to the building's main gate. I could see a man hiding behind the table. I became suspicious and asked him what he was doing.""The man ran away semi-naked with his trouser and underwear in his hand.I chased him but taking advantage of the darkness amid heavy rains, he escaped towards the highway."She added, "I called my father downstairs after informing about the incident. We closely checked the dog and found her bleeding from private part. Also, there was human semen on the floor behind the table. I fed the dog and contacted a volunteer of an NGO Jeevan Foundation Yuva Sena, Animal Welfare Force in Kharghar.""I arranged a cab for the volunteer, who took the injured dog to Panvel Panchayat Samiti's Animal Husbandry department, opposite Panvel ST bus depot, where the government veterinarian confirmed sexual assault on the dog, who was treated for the injuries. Hence, I registered an FIR against the unidentified accused man for sexually assaulting the female stray dog and causing injury to her private part.""Our building's CCTV footage shows the accused man running away from the building, but just because the street lights were not working, his image was not clearly visible. We are retrieving more CCTV footages from other shops in our building for providing them to Ulwe police."PSI Rama Dhavare of Ulwe said, "After registering an FIR, the forensic team collected the human semen sample and hair strands from the crime scene. Once the accused is arrested, the DNA match will be the vital evidence in court for conviction of the accused."
Article Summary: The incident occurred outside a tea shop on the ground floor in Siddhivinayak Platinum society in sector 23, Ulwe on Sunday around 11.45pm. The unidentified accused was booked under BNS section and Prevention of Cruelty to Animal.

Article Title: 9 woman rescued from flesh trade in Taloja lodge, 3 accused held
Article Text:
The crime branch team arrested three accused including the lodge manager and two waiters.

NAVI MUMBAI: The Anti-Human Trafficking Unit (AHTU) of Navi Mumbai crime branch busted a prostitution racket at hotel-cum lodge in Taloja and rescued nine women from the flesh trade on July 18. The crime branch team arrested three accused including the lodge manager and two waiters.Gajanan Kadam, senior inspector of AHTU said, "As per the information received about prostitution being carried out at Hotel Abode Inn Lodging and Boarding in Taloja, we set a trap by sending a decoy customer, whom the lodge manager provided a woman for sexual favour for Rs 3,000 that was accepted by one waiter. On the signal of the customer customer, we raided the lodge, where 9 women were kept for prostitution. The lodge manager Balram Gowda, waiters Girish Pujari and Krishnaraj Patil were arrested for dragging the women into prostitution. An FIR was registered at Taloja police station against the three arrested accused Gowda, Pujari and Patil, who were booked relevant BNS sections and Prevention of Immoral Trafficking Act. The Panvel court remanded them to police custody till July 21. The rescued women were sent to women's shelter home as directed by the magistrate."
Article Summary: The Anti-Human Trafficking Unit of Navi Mumbai crime branch busted a prostitution racket at hotel-cum lodge in Taloja. The crime branch team arrested three accused including the lodge manager and two waiters. The lodge manager Balram Gowda, waiters Girish Pujari and Krishnaraj Patil were arrested.

Article Title: Truck driver arrested from Gujarat for killing fellow driver with iron rod over caste dispute in Maharashtra
Article Text:
Taloja police have caught a truck driver involved in the tragic murder of a fellow driver during a dispute fueled by caste discrimination (Representative image)

NAVI MUMBAI: Taloja police have arrested a 40-year-old truck driver who had absconded after fatally assaulting a 45-year-old truck driver on his head with an iron rod in the truck parking lot of Nisha Transport company in Nitlas village near Taloja industrial area in Panvel taluka on July 14 early morning.The accused was arrested from Valsad railway station, Gujarat on Friday, while he was escaping by train to his home town in UP.The arrested accused has been identified as Ramesh Kumar Yadav and the murder victim as Chandan Pandey, both hailing from UP.Sagar Nikam, PI (crime) of Taloja said, "The murder was an outcome of the Pandey versus Yadav caste discrimination, especially in UP. The accused Yadav had fatally assaulted the victim Pandey as the latter being a Brahmin used to humiliate Yadav from OBC by treating him as inferior, as claimed by the accused Yadav."PI Nikam informed, "On Monday night, an argument has ensued between Pandey and Yadav in the parking lot over caste discrimination. As they quarrelled, the other truck drivers intervened and resolved the matter. On Tuesday around 5.30 am, again both of them quarrelled, when Yadav assaulted on Pandey's head with an iron rod that proved fatal.""Pandey escaped after threatening other truckers if they attempted to catch him. The security guard Mohammad Alam Hajif-ul Khan (58) informed the police. Pandey was rushed to Panvel sub-district hospital where he was declared brought dead. Subsequently, a murder case was registered against the accused Yadav. His photograph found in his parked truck was immediately circulated to the GRP and RPF at railway stations where multiple trains heading to UP halt.""On Friday, the Valsad GRP informed us that Yadav has been detained at Valsad railway station while he was travelling in an express train to escape to his hometown in UP. Our police team reached Valsad and arrested Yadav. The Panvel JMFC court has remanded Yadav to police custody untill July 21."
Article Summary: Ramesh Kumar Yadav, 40, was arrested from Valsad railway station, Gujarat on Friday. He had absconded after fatally assaulting a 45-year-old truck driver on his head with an iron rod. The murder was an outcome of the Pandey versus Yadav caste discrimination, especially in UP.
